agent-orchestration-before-searching-ass.rule: Before searching assumed public entry-file paths, enumerate the repository files with rg --files and search only paths that actually exist.

agent-orchestration-resolve-named-skill-.rule: Resolve named skill paths from the supplied skill-roots table before reading SKILL.md; never assume a project-local .agentsmesh/skills path.

agent-orchestration-when-dispatching-a-r.rule: When dispatching a read-only or review subagent, do NOT give it tools that can mutate state — no shell that can run `git checkout`/`git reset`/`git restore`, no file deletes or overwrites. Use a read-only tool profile (e.g. the Explore agent type), confine experimental writes to a fresh temp dir the subagent creates, and commit or stash before fan-out so a stray revert stays recoverable.

agent-orchestration-when-spawning-a-suba.rule: When spawning a subagent with fork_context=true, omit agent_type, model, and reasoning_effort because the full-history fork inherits them.

ci-and-release-security-rule-1.rule: **Never interpolate `${{ ... }}` directly into `run:` script bodies for any expression carrying user-influenceable data (CWE-78).** Flow inputs/outputs through `env:` so they become shell variables, then validate shape (e.g. `case "$VERSION" in [!0-9]*|*[!a-zA-Z0-9.+-]*|"") exit 1 ;; esac`) before use. Applies to `inputs.*`, `steps.*.outputs.*`, and `needs.*.outputs.*` that transitively trace to a workflow input.

ci-and-release-security-rule-10.rule: **Post-publish `git tag` steps must be idempotent.** `changeset publish` already creates a local `v<version>` tag for single-package repos regardless of the `commit:` flag. The post-publish step shape: `git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$TAG" >/dev/null || git tag "$TAG"; git push origin "$TAG"`.

ci-and-release-security-rule-11.rule: **`.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf` (plus explicit categories for `*.md`, `*.json`, `*.yaml`) is mandatory in any cross-platform repo whose tests stage fixtures into temp dirs and assert byte-stable generated artifacts.** Windows runners default to `core.autocrlf=true`; relying on per-runner git config is not a contract. Fix EOL at the repo boundary via attributes, not at every consumer site.

ci-and-release-security-rule-12.rule: **CI workflows must run `pnpm build` before any job invoking `pnpm test` or `pnpm test:coverage` when the test config includes integration tests that exec `dist/cli.js`.** Only `pnpm test:e2e` self-builds; the others do not. Fresh CI clones have no prior `dist/`.

ci-and-release-security-rule-13.rule: **Tests/integration steps must never hardcode `/bin/sh` or `/bin/zsh` once Windows is in the CI matrix; never use shell-based `2>&1` redirection in test runners.** Use `spawnSync(process.execPath, [...args])` and concatenate `result.stdout + result.stderr`. On Linux `ubuntu-latest`, `/bin/zsh` does not exist; on Windows neither does `/bin/sh`.

ci-and-release-security-rule-14.rule: **Tests that stub `git` via a `chmod 755` Node script or pass `NODE_OPTIONS=--import=<unix path>` must be `it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')`.** GitHub Actions Windows runners block git network ops and do not honor these stub strategies. Cover the behavior on Linux/macOS.

ci-and-release-security-rule-15.rule: **Plugin/source classifiers distinguishing "local file" from "npm specifier" must accept Windows drive-letter absolutes (`/^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]/`) alongside POSIX `/...`, `./...`, `../...`, and `file:`.** `node:path.resolve()` on win32 produces `D:\foo`; missing this routes legitimate absolute paths into `resolveNpmSpecifier` and `import()` fails.

ci-and-release-security-rule-16.rule: **Test assertions that a tracked file ships executable must query the git index (`git ls-files --stage <path>` and match `/^100755 /`), not `statSync(...).mode & 0o111`.** NTFS on Windows runners does not surface POSIX execute bits; the git-index mode is what `gh release create` carries into the tarball.

ci-and-release-security-rule-2.rule: **Dependent jobs that must run when an upstream is conditionally skipped need an explicit status-function override.** Use `if: !cancelled() && (needs.<upstream>.result == 'success' && <cond> || <skip-allowed-cond>)`. Prefer `!cancelled()` over `always()`. The default implicit `success()` on `if:` short-circuits whenever the upstream was skipped.

ci-and-release-security-rule-3.rule: **Never embed tokens in git remote URLs.** Use `actions/checkout@v4` with `repository:` + `token:` so the credential helper handles auth per-process. Token-in-URL leaks into `.git/config`, `ps`/`/proc/$pid/cmdline`, and uploaded workspace artifacts; GitHub Actions log redaction does NOT cover these surfaces.

ci-and-release-security-rule-4.rule: **Pin every tool that produces release artifacts to at least major.minor; never `latest` in a release pipeline.** Applies to `setup-bun` (`bun-version: "1.2"`), Docker image tags, `npm install` in CI, and any other tool acquisition step in release builds. Reserve `latest` for dev-only iteration.

ci-and-release-security-rule-5.rule: **Checksum verification in curl|sh installers must fail closed (CWE-345).** Both "expected hash absent/empty" and "no checksum tool available" branches must `error` (exit non-zero), never `warn` and continue. The user installing a checksum tool is the right trade-off.

ci-and-release-security-rule-6.rule: **Validate env-controlled paths against a strict allowlist before they cross into shell-parsed files (CWE-77).** Any value flowing from env into a file that is later parsed by a shell (rc files, sourced configs) is shell-equivalent input. Reject anything outside `[a-zA-Z0-9./_~\ -]` for installer paths. Threat model is wrapping processes (Docker entrypoints, Makefiles, parent installers), not the user.

ci-and-release-security-rule-7.rule: **Use `awk` field-equality, not `grep` substring, to look up values keyed by exact filename in checksum-style manifests.** `grep "$TARGET" SHA256SUMS | awk '{print $1}'` matches `agentsmesh-darwin-arm64.exe` and `$TARGET.sig` lines too; use `awk -v t="$TARGET" '$2==t {print $1}'`. Same rule for any `<token>  <filename>` manifest.

ci-and-release-security-rule-8.rule: **Installer scripts editing shell-rc files MUST branch the written line by shell, not just the file path.** Key both the rc-file path AND the line content off `$SHELL`: fish needs `fish_add_path -gP "$BIN_DIR"` (or `set -gx PATH "$BIN_DIR" $PATH`); bash/zsh use `export PATH=...`. Also `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$config")"` before `>>` because parent dirs (e.g. `~/.config/fish/`) may not exist.

ci-and-release-security-rule-9.rule: **For npm trusted publishing, choose a GitHub-hosted Node version whose bundled npm already satisfies current docs; do not self-upgrade npm in CI.** `npm install -g npm@latest` fails on `ubuntu-latest` with arborist dependency tree breakage before the publish step runs. Add an explicit npm install only when a specific known-good version is needed AND the runner cannot supply it directly.

dist-backed-tests-rule-1.rule: Run `pnpm build` before any targeted e2e or integration slice whenever source affecting `dist/cli.js` has changed; ad hoc `vitest` runs do not auto-build (Evidence L114, L116, L165).

dist-backed-tests-rule-2.rule: Never run two CLI commands that read or rebuild `dist/` in parallel — serialize anything that touches `dist/cli.js` or runs `pnpm build`, since `tsup` cleans `dist/` at build start and concurrent workers will hit ENOENT/MODULE_NOT_FOUND mid-test (Evidence L57, L115).

dist-backed-tests-rule-3.rule: Before declaring a dist-backed failure a product bug, rebuild and rerun — stale `dist/cli.js` will surface as missing generated prompts or implementation regressions that do not exist in source (Evidence L116, L165).

dist-backed-tests-rule-4.rule: In `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, place `pnpm build` BEFORE `pnpm test` and `pnpm test:coverage` whenever those configs include integration files that exec `dist/cli.js`; only `pnpm test:e2e` self-builds (`pnpm build && vitest run --config ...`) (Evidence L187).

dist-backed-tests-rule-5.rule: Keep `runCli`/e2e CLI helper timeouts comfortably above targeted-run latency so full-suite parallel pressure does not exceed the 30s budget; reproduce timeout-looking failures both targeted and under the full runner before treating them as product behavior failures (Evidence L53).

dist-backed-tests-rule-6.rule: When refactoring cache-backed features that dist-backed tests exercise (remote extends, refresh), preserve existing on-disk cache paths for supported providers unless an explicit migration is added and verified — changing GitHub cache-key layout breaks refresh tests that look in the prior directory (Evidence L119).

dist-backed-tests-rule-7.rule: Unit tests that call `runGenerate`/`runWatch` directly (same process) contribute to coverage; dist-backed integration tests that exec a subprocess do not — pick the harness intentionally when targeting coverage gaps (Evidence L109).

dist-backed-tests-when-committing-untrac.rule: When committing untracked files in this repo (e.g. QA reports under tasks/reports/), know the precommit hook runs `pnpm test:coverage`, whose run deletes untracked files in the real working tree — `git add` then a separate `git commit` will silently drop them. Stage the files and commit docs-only changes with `--no-verify`, or fix the offending test to write only under a temp dir. Tracked files survive; only untracked ones are removed.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-1.rule: Assert the exact relative path set and exact count for generated files/dirs — never `some(...)`, prefix matches, or "at least one". Cross-check referenced artifacts (e.g. hook wrapper scripts) against the config that points to them.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-10.rule: When replacing or removing a core helper API, run a targeted search for all direct imports/usages (including unit tests that reference helpers by name like the old reference normalizer) and update those tests before relying on the full suite.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-11.rule: Whenever a generation/import/rewrite contract changes, mirror updates across the matching suites: research (`agents-folder-structure-research`), round-trip (`import-generate-roundtrip`), edge-case (`link-rebaser-edge-cases`), unit, integration, and e2e — primary tests alone do not codify the full contract.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-12.rule: Use the correct shape for test helpers: `findGeneratedFile` accepts either a plain string for exact path matching or `{ stringContaining }`/`{ stringMatching }` — `{ exactPath }` does not exist. Check the helper's actual parameter types before use.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-13.rule: For global-mode structure validation tests, drive `generate()` from `src/core/generate/engine.ts` with `scope: 'global'` and a `ValidatedConfig`-shaped fixture — `runGenerate()` from the CLI returns an exit code, not files.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-14.rule: Cross-platform assertion tolerance: normalize native paths to POSIX in tests via `toPosixPath(result.fromPath)` before `.toContain('.codex/...')`; extend `stripProtectedRegions` to drop Windows absolute-path tokens before `not.toContain('.agentsmesh\\')` checks; permit any of `` `docs/...` ``, `` `/docs/...` ``, `` `./docs/...` ``, `` `../docs/...` `` for inline-backtick path rewrites that depend on realpath on 8.3-shortname Windows tmpdirs.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-15.rule: When codegen-ing module-level array-literal data from per-target imports, patch the existing source file in place between sentinel comments instead of extracting to a new generated module — `descriptor-paths.test.ts` and other per-descriptor import paths trip ESM TDZ when an extra hop captures undefined slots.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-16.rule: Per-target import mappers referenced from a descriptor object literal must live in a third file (`import-mappers.ts`), never in `importer.ts` — descriptor↔importer cycles capture `undefined` in `map:` fields and the runner throws at execution time.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-2.rule: When asserting an exact generated repo tree after `generate`, include `.agentsmesh/.lock` in the expected set — `generate` always emits it.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-3.rule: When a user asks for e2e coverage over realistic structures, start from the richest existing fixture and mutate a temp copy — do not invent a smaller synthetic project.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-4.rule: Audit fixtures with a full-depth listing first; never use `find -maxdepth N` on nested skill/reference trees and conclude content is absent.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-5.rule: Before writing parameterized tests, scoring rules, or tie-breaks over any descriptor-derived list (`BUILTIN_TARGETS`, `RULES`, capability sets), run a one-shot `tsx scripts/<dump>.mts` that materializes the values and counts collisions; pick inputs that are unique per case and document ambiguity.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-6.rule: Re-import tests must cover importing into an *existing* `.agentsmesh` tree, not only empty-project round trips — verify unsupported target metadata is preserved from the canonical destination instead of erased.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-7.rule: When converting loose install/manifest assertions into strict ones, inspect the real persisted entry shape first and lock tests to the observed contract (field omission, ordering) — never write expectations from inferred intent.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-8.rule: Mock `ValidatedConfig` fixtures (any `mockLoadScopedConfig.mockResolvedValue(...)`) must include every field the schema defaults populate (e.g. `plugins: []`). When a new orchestration step reads `config.X`, grep every mock and add the field before rerunning.

fixture-and-assertion-discipline-rule-9.rule: When tightening `TargetDescriptor` schema requirements, run a repo-wide descriptor fixture search plus the full test suite and update every plugin/mock descriptor fixture to the full contract — focused catalog tests are insufficient.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-1.rule: Every third-party YAML frontmatter parse on install/import paths — whether the file is `SKILL.md`, command, agent, rule, MDC, or skill-name extraction (`readSkillFrontmatterName()`) — MUST use `tryParseFrontmatter()` / `parseFrontmatterForPath(..., onError)` and emit a "skipping <path>: <reason>" warning on failure. Reserve strict `parseFrontmatter()` exclusively for user-authored canonical content under `.agentsmesh/`.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-2.rule: When auditing parser changes, grep both `parseFrontmatter` AND every per-target importer (`src/targets/<id>/importer*.ts`) plus every auxiliary helper (skill-name extraction, MDC inference, name detection) before declaring the lenient-parsing fix applied.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-3.rule: NEVER add files under `.agentsmesh/skills/<name>/` beyond `SKILL.md` and ordinary supporting files (`references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`, `assets/`). Do not invent `agents/openai.yaml` or other shapes — the canonical skill spec is `SKILL.md` + supporting files only.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-4.rule: NEVER write a literal `*/` inside any `/* ... */` or JSDoc block comment — including header comments in test files. Replace glob-shaped paths in prose (e.g. `.agentsmesh/skills/*/SKILL.md`) with `skills/{name}/SKILL.md` or `glob: *.md`, or move the glob into a single-line `//` comment outside the block.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-5.rule: Canonical booleans derivable from the destination path or artifact kind (notably `root: false` on non-root rules) MUST be derived and serialized in one shared helper, never left to per-target importer habits. Add cross-target tests that assert the exact canonical frontmatter contract.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-6.rule: Manual install staging and persistence MUST share one skill-name derivation helper. If staging reads the name via `readSkillFrontmatterName()` from `SKILL.md` frontmatter, persistence (`pick.skills`) MUST use the same source — never `basename(contentRoot)` on one side and frontmatter on the other.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-7.rule: Any synthetic canonical entity created from a non-frontmattered source (e.g. `.cursorrules` / `.windsurfrules` root files, marketplace stubs) MUST carry a non-empty `description` (e.g. `Imported from .cursorrules`). Empty descriptions pass unit tests but get dropped by `resolveRulePool()`'s `validateRule` re-filter under `dryRun=true`, even with `--force`.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-8.rule: Projected-agent test fixtures MUST be built from the documented `serializeProjectedAgentSkill()` output: real `x-agentsmesh-kind: agent` plus `x-agentsmesh-name` (or an `am-agent-*` directory). NEVER invent flags like `x-projected-agent: true`. Assertions must lock the exact canonical `.agentsmesh/agents/<name>.md` destination.

frontmatter-and-canonical-shapes-rule-9.rule: Filter "boilerplate" files by intent, not by a single blanket predicate. Maintain one typed map (`stem → 'noise' | 'preserved'`) with three derived predicates: `isBoilerplate` (prevent phantom entities in entity importers / flat-collection classifiers), `isNoiseBoilerplate` (drop in staging + skill supporting-files), `isPreservedBoilerplate` (keep LICENSE/NOTICE/COPYING/README in skill subtrees AND at pack root for legal attribution + consumer context). Both `listSupportingFiles` and `cpFilteredSkill` must use the noise-only predicate at content-staging time.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-1.rule: Whenever a target generates more than one file from the same canonical source, audit the output-source map against the full generator output list so every emitted path participates in rewriting and collision logic — never assume "one canonical → one artifact".

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-10.rule: When an importer maps reserved/generated source artifacts back into canonical files, add strict re-import tests that preseed stale outputs (`_ab-agent-*`, `_ab-command-*`, hidden scoped rules) and verify the importer removes them — import is not write-only.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-11.rule: When two targets implement the same import filter/cleanup pattern (e.g. Codex and Windsurf), move the logic into a shared helper and verify both targets against the same strict regression cases — never copy-paste per-target cleanup.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-12.rule: When importing any target artifact, build the normalization map from every supported generated path family so re-import can recover canonical `.agentsmesh/...` links from previously polluted outputs (e.g. cline / claude-code reading Codex-style `.agents/...` links). Never assume same-family pristine inputs.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-13.rule: When one canonical feature emits multiple artifact families (e.g. Copilot hook JSON + wrapper scripts), centralize the eligibility predicate ("is this hook runnable?") in one shared helper and add a regression test comparing referenced artifacts against emitted files. Never duplicate "is valid" logic per generator.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-14.rule: When a target generator intentionally drops canonical metadata (e.g. Codex CLI MCP `description`), add or update a target-specific lint warning and cover with unit + CLI e2e tests; unsupported metadata is part of the target contract users must see.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-15.rule: When tests verify generated files or directories, assert the exact relative path set and exact count, and cross-check referenced artifacts (e.g. hook wrapper scripts) against the config that points to them — no `some(...)`, prefix-only, or "at least one" checks.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-16.rule: When a target-format cannot represent all canonical metadata (e.g. Cursor command `description`/`allowed-tools`), add strict re-import-into-existing-project tests that prove unsupported fields are preserved from the canonical destination rather than erased. Empty-project round trips are insufficient.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-17.rule: When widening a core type into a union (e.g. `McpServer` gaining URL transports), add explicit type guards at every serializer/generator boundary that needs a specific variant and rerun `pnpm typecheck` before declaring the refactor done.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-18.rule: In `resolveGen` (engine), check `getBuiltinTargetDefinition(target)` first; if present, delegate entirely to `resolveTargetFeatureGenerator(target, feature, config)` so conversion config (e.g. `commandsToSkills: false`) is always respected. Plugin registry fallback must not bypass builtin conversion logic via `getDescriptor`.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-19.rule: When a command validates multiple canonical features in `runLint()`, gate each lint family (commands, MCP, permissions, hooks) by its own feature flag — never nest them all under `hasRules`. Add a regression test for configs that enable non-rule features without `rules`.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-2.rule: When a layout declares `additionalRootDecorationPaths`, add those decoration paths to generate-side source maps and test at least one nested Markdown mirror for canonical link cleanup; decoration paths are generated artifacts, not render-only metadata.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-20.rule: When multiple targets share a common parent directory in global mode (e.g. `.gemini/`), each non-native target must use a namespaced subdirectory (Antigravity → `.gemini/antigravity/`) to avoid path collisions; the collision detector only special-cases `AGENTS.md`.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-3.rule: When a target can emit multiple artifact families from the same canonical source (e.g. Copilot `.github/copilot/*.instructions.md` and `.github/instructions/*.md`), build and cache rewrite maps per output path or per artifact family — never key only by target. Add tests for each emitted path family.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-4.rule: When resolving conflicting shared artifacts by choosing a preferred/richer content body, keep that chosen result's `status`/`currentContent`; only merge statuses for truly identical content. Never let a discarded result donate drift status to the kept artifact.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-5.rule: When multiple targets share one output path, compare outputs after normalizing target-specific references back to canonical paths before deciding they conflict; add coverage for rewritten-content overlaps.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-6.rule: When skills can originate from packs, add pack-path→target-path entries to the artifact map (alongside canonical `.agentsmesh/skills/...` entries) so the reference rewriter can translate both canonical and pack absolute paths.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-7.rule: When appending global instructions / root-instruction decoration to generated targets, phrase the canonical location without the literal `.agentsmesh/` substring (e.g. "the `.agentsmesh` directory at the project root"), keep legacy paragraph detection for upgrades, and strip both old and new contract blocks on import in the shared root-rule import path. Cover with round-trip e2e.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-8.rule: When adding a secondary rule projection folder for a target that already has a primary root file (e.g. Codex `AGENTS.md`), default to mirroring only non-root / additional rules — never duplicate the primary root file unless the spec explicitly requires it.

generation-collision-source-maps-rule-9.rule: When enabling a new artifact family for a target, update `reference-map-targets` + import-reference map builders + importer scanners together; do not ship generator/importer surface files first and patch path-translation contracts later. Verify with the target-contract matrix e2e.

global-mode-rule-1.rule: When implementing global mode for any target, add a `global` layout AND `rewriteGeneratedPath` that translates project-level paths (e.g. `.github/`) to global paths (e.g. `.copilot/`). Layout path resolvers alone are not enough — the engine uses `rewriteGeneratedPath` to transform generator output paths before writing. Verify a representative file lands at the correct global location.

global-mode-rule-10.rule: For global-mode structure-validation tests, call `generate()` from `src/core/generate/engine.ts` with `scope: 'global'` — not `runGenerate()` from the CLI commands, which returns an exit code (`Promise<number>`) instead of the generated files. Provide a `makeConfig()` helper returning a `ValidatedConfig` with target + features configured.

global-mode-rule-11.rule: Derive global-mode e2e expectations from each target's descriptor/layout constants (e.g. Windsurf `workflows`, Roo `.roo-code`, Codex `config.toml`), not from historical path helpers. Whenever a path-rewrite helper is retired or global behavior shifts, update e2e assertions from descriptor constants and rerun the e2e Vitest config after `pnpm build`.

global-mode-rule-12.rule: Keep canonical loader helpers (e.g. `loadCanonicalFiles()`) backward-compatible with BOTH project-root and canonical-dir inputs when adding scope awareness. Sweep every caller before tightening the signature — extend, install, and the loader test suite all pass project roots and expect the helper to locate `.agentsmesh/` itself.

global-mode-rule-13.rule: When bridging generated global files into an importer fallback path in tests, copy the EXACT generated tree the round-trip needs — including `references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`, and `assets/` — not just `SKILL.md`.

global-mode-rule-14.rule: For `findGeneratedFile` in global structure tests, pass a plain string for exact path matching or an object with `stringContaining`/`stringMatching`. Never invent `{ exactPath: '...' }` — check the actual signature first.

global-mode-rule-2.rule: Follow the full global-mode pattern in one pass: (a) global path constants, (b) `global` layout with `rewriteGeneratedPath`, (c) `mirrorGlobalPath` for cross-agent skill mirroring, (d) `globalCapabilities`, (e) `globalDetectionPaths`, (f) help text + docs. Model from Copilot/Cursor/Roo Code. Update all six together.

global-mode-rule-3.rule: After editing a target's `rewriteGeneratedPath`/global layout, re-audit imports — every referenced constant (e.g. `CURSOR_COMPAT_AGENTS`) must be in the file's import list. Run `pnpm typecheck` and the target's `generate --global` CLI test; treat missing-symbol imports as a release gate.

global-mode-rule-4.rule: When implementing global mode, import every required type (`TargetCapabilities`, `TargetLayout`) from `target.interface.js` and run `pnpm typecheck` immediately after adding the global layout. Do not assume copy-pasted patterns carried all imports.

global-mode-rule-5.rule: Namespace global paths under shared parent directories so multiple targets do not collide. If multiple targets share `.gemini/`, `.agents/`, etc., each non-native one MUST use a namespaced subdirectory (e.g. Antigravity → `.gemini/antigravity/`, Gemini CLI native → `.gemini/`). The collision detector only special-cases `AGENTS.md`; other shared-path collisions throw.

global-mode-rule-6.rule: In `import` flows, when `scope === 'global'`, only read tool-native subtrees under the home root (e.g. `~/.codex`, `~/.agents/skills`). Never run whole-tree `readDirRecursive` / `importFileDirectory` from `homedir()` — that blows the stack on symlink cycles (e.g. `~/.cache`) and scans the entire home tree. Add a `scope === 'global'` guard.

global-mode-rule-7.rule: In any helper that fakes the home directory via env (`HOME`) for `--global` e2e, on `process.platform === 'win32'` ALSO set `USERPROFILE` (and defensively `HOMEDRIVE`/`HOMEPATH`) from the same path, because `os.homedir()` on Windows reads `USERPROFILE`, not `HOME`. Put this in the spawn helper, not at call sites.

global-mode-rule-8.rule: For temp-dir symlink helpers that stage a fake home (e.g. `createTempProjectRoot(homedir())`), only symlink dot-entries (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, …) and root-level files. Never symlink non-dot directories like `Desktop`/`Documents` — listings/walks over the project root (`listScopedAgentsFiles`, the 18-target normalizer) will traverse them and hang.

global-mode-rule-9.rule: For `mirrorGlobalPath` skip/dual-mirror tests, derive eligibility from the run's actively-generated targets, not the configured set. `feature-loop.ts` passes the post-filter `targets` array to `mirrorGlobalPath`; using `targetFilter: ['copilot']` removes codex-cli from "active" even when it is in `config.targets`. To exercise the codex-cli skip, list both targets in `config.targets` and DO NOT pass `targetFilter`.

install-import-pickers-rule-1.rule: Treat `as` on `InstallTarget` as a routing decision, not a feature label. Only set `as` for **flat-collection** sub-packs (no `skillPack`/`rootSkill` marker); leave `as` undefined for skill-pack / root-skill sub-packs so recursion re-runs auto-discovery at the sub-pack root. Always plumb `report.subPackFailures` into `InstallData` so the CLI renderer surfaces partial failures.

install-import-pickers-rule-10.rule: Manual install persistence and staging must share one skill-name derivation. If staging uses `readSkillFrontmatterName()`, persistence must use the same helper — never `basename(contentRoot)`.

install-import-pickers-rule-11.rule: When manual skill replay carries `pick.skills: [name]` but `path` is a collection root (e.g. `skills` or `skills/engineering`), search **all descendant `SKILL.md` paths** under the source root and stage the exact matched skill directories. Don't restrict to umbrella folders that themselves have `SKILL.md`.

install-import-pickers-rule-12.rule: Replay/scoped install narrowing must reach `installAsPack()` — pass the narrowed canonical through every downstream write/materialization path so unrelated settings (`mcp`, `permissions`, `hooks`, `ignore`) don't leak into the resulting pack.

install-import-pickers-rule-13.rule: Provide an explicit `--as` override that bypasses native-path heuristics; keep native auto-detection as fallback. Install discovery must not be coupled to target-native directory layouts for arbitrary folders.

install-import-pickers-rule-14.rule: Native install discovery is **read-only staging**. Import into a temporary staged copy and derive folder/file scope from importer `fromPath` results — never mutate the source checkout or heuristically traverse it for subtree selection.

install-import-pickers-rule-15.rule: Incremental pack updates must match by **stable remote identity** (provider + repo/url without ref), not the pinned `github:org/repo@sha`. Refresh stored `source`/`version` metadata after each successful merge. Preserve existing on-disk cache paths when refactoring cache-backed providers.

install-import-pickers-rule-16.rule: Single-file remote install parsing must cover both `tree/...` (directory) and `blob/...` (file) URLs per supported host.

install-import-pickers-rule-17.rule: Pack coverage must include settings features (`mcp`, `permissions`, `hooks`, `ignore`) — not just array resources. Write → load → generate tests must include a real non-dry-run command path.

install-import-pickers-rule-18.rule: Synthetic root-rule canonical entries (`.cursorrules`, `.windsurfrules`, marketplace stubs) MUST carry a non-empty `description` (e.g. `Imported from .cursorrules`) so they survive the dry-run-only re-validation pass in `pool-resolution.ts` (`resolveRulePool` filters by `validateRule` when `dryRun=true`).

install-import-pickers-rule-19.rule: Boilerplate filtering splits intent via one typed map (`stem → 'noise' | 'preserved'`) and three derived predicates: `isBoilerplate` (any — used by entity importers + flat-collection classifier to prevent README/LICENSE from becoming phantom entities), `isNoiseBoilerplate` (drop in staging + skill supporting-files), `isPreservedBoilerplate` (keep in skill subtrees). Both `listSupportingFiles` (canonical/features/skills.ts) AND `cpFilteredSkill` (install/source/skill-repo-filter.ts) must use the noise-only predicate at content-staging time.

install-import-pickers-rule-2.rule: Every third-party frontmatter parser on the install/import path — including auxiliary helpers like skill-name extraction (`readSkillFrontmatterName`) and `.mdc` inference (`inferMdcTarget`, `normalizeMdcToCanonical`) — must use `tryParseFrontmatter()` / `parseFrontmatterForPath(..., onError)` and degrade with a "skipping <path>: <reason>" warning. Reserve strict `parseFrontmatter()` for user-authored canonical content. Audit by grepping both `parseFrontmatter` and every `src/targets/<id>/importer*.ts`.

install-import-pickers-rule-20.rule: Plumb upstream `contentRoot` end-to-end (`runSinglePackInstall → executeRunInstallPoolsAndWrite → installAsPack → materializePack/mergeIntoPack`) so `collectPreservedRootFiles(contentRoot)` harvests top-level `README*` / `LICENSE*` / `NOTICE*` / `COPYING*` / `COPYRIGHT*` into the pack root **before** `hashPackContent` runs — preserved files must participate in `content_hash` + the per-file install manifest so uninstall removes them automatically.

install-import-pickers-rule-21.rule: `OUTPUT_DIR_TO_FEATURE` and `stripMarkdownExt` in `src/core/reference/validate-generated-markdown-links.ts` must enumerate every target-specific dir (`droids`, `instructions`, `prompts`, `steering`, …) and every double-extension (`.agent.md`, `.instructions.md`, `.prompt.md`) so `canonicalKeyFromOutputPath` produces the same canonical key as the source entity. Treat as a single-source-of-truth table: new target = one row each.

install-import-pickers-rule-22.rule: Wrap the terminal `runGenerate()` in **both** `runInstall` and `runUninstall` in try/catch (extracted as `runPostOperationGenerate('install' | 'uninstall', scope, rootBase)` in `src/install/run/post-install-generate.ts`). Downgrade failures to `logger.warn(...)` naming the failure mode — the pack + `installs.yaml` writes are the user's intent and must survive validator brittleness. Same rule for any future best-effort post-operation step (e.g. post-install `agentsmesh lint`).

install-import-pickers-rule-23.rule: Per-target skill-import dispatch loops belong behind one `importSkillsDirectory(options, recognizers[])` orchestrator with factory recognizers (`projectedAgentRecognizer`, `commandSkillRecognizer`) that own their own destination write + stale cleanup. Per-target adapters collapse to a config object + recognizer list so new targets can't drift on cleanup order or recognizer ordering.

install-import-pickers-rule-24.rule: When persisting strict install manifest assertions, inspect the **actual serialized entry shape** first (including field omission and ordering) — don't write expectations from inferred intent. Whenever the manifest type gains required fields, sweep all `toHaveBeenCalledWith` / deep-equality assertions, not just the typed fixture.

install-import-pickers-rule-25.rule: Whenever pack/install manifest persistence semantics change, rerun the full agents/commands/rules/skills matrix and the sibling-item amend cases — not only the user-reported entity.

install-import-pickers-rule-26.rule: Skill-pack integration fixtures with broken links must narrow the project's `features:` so the linking entity is NOT generated (e.g. `features: [rules]` when the broken link sits in a skill). Assert pack body + manifest there, not generated target files. Cross-protocol identity assertions (https/ssh/`github:` shorthand) belong in unit tests on `findExistingInstallName`, not integration.

install-import-pickers-rule-27.rule: Mock `ValidatedConfig` fixtures returned by `mockLoadScopedConfig.mockResolvedValue` must include every schema-defaulted field (`plugins: []`, etc.) because tests bypass schema validation. Adding any new orchestration step that reads `config.X` requires grepping for every mock and adding the field before rerunning.

install-import-pickers-rule-28.rule: Global import (`scope === 'global'`) must NOT pass `homedir()` as `projectRoot` for recursive scans. Only read tool-native subtrees under home (e.g. `~/.codex`, `~/.agents/skills`); never `readDirRecursive(homedir())` — symlink cycles under `~/.cache` will blow the stack.

install-import-pickers-rule-29.rule: Importers must clean stale reserved artifacts on re-import (e.g. `_ab-agent-*`, `_ab-command-*`, scoped-rule names). Extract shared filter/cleanup into one helper instead of copy-pasting per target. Import normalization must build the rewrite map from **every supported generated path family** so cross-target re-import recovers canonical `.agentsmesh/...` links from previously polluted outputs.

install-import-pickers-rule-3.rule: Normalize empty-string CLI flags (`path`, `target`, `as`) to `undefined` inside `readInstallFlags`. Picker auto-pick recursion in `run-install-locked.ts` builds nested flag bags with `target ?? ''`; the rest of the pipeline assumes "undefined OR non-empty".

install-import-pickers-rule-30.rule: When a target-native filename changes, update generation/docs to the new path but keep importer fallbacks for the previous on-disk filename unless the migration is explicitly destructive.

install-import-pickers-rule-31.rule: Per-target import mappers (custom `ImportEntryMapper`) MUST live in `<target>/import-mappers.ts` — never in `importer.ts`. Putting them in `importer.ts` and importing from `index.ts` forms a cycle: `index.ts → importer.ts → index.ts`, and the descriptor's object literal captures `undefined` for `map:` fields. Function references stored as descriptor fields are safe (live bindings); object literals capturing those references at module-init are not. Establish `import-mappers.ts` even for one mapper.

install-import-pickers-rule-32.rule: Don't migrate an `ignore` (or any single-output) feature to descriptor `flatFile` mode without re-reading the original importer. `flatFile` writes the FIRST `source` path verbatim — it never merges/dedupes. If the original concatenates multiple files (e.g. cursor merges `.cursorignore` + `.cursorindexingignore`), keep it imperative or extend the runner with `mergedFlatFile`.

install-import-pickers-rule-33.rule: `isLocalSource` for plugin paths must accept Windows drive-letter absolutes — match `/^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]/` alongside POSIX (`/…`, `./…`, `../…`, `file:`). Tests that build absolute paths with `resolve()` and feed them as plugin `source` exercise this.

install-import-pickers-rule-4.rule: Marketplace `--all` recursive installs must omit `--as` (only pass `--path` and `--target`) — `targetFromSubPack`'s first-feature inference forces the manual single-kind path which rejects mixed-content sub-packs.

install-import-pickers-rule-5.rule: Lower the picker's marketplace-branch threshold to `subPacks.length >= 1` when sub-packs come from explicit sources like `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`. Singleton plugin lists must route through the marketplace branch, not `runSinglePackInstall` against an empty root. The directory-heuristic detector keeps its own `>= 2` floor.

install-import-pickers-rule-6.rule: Nested `runInstall` calls from picker auto-pick (single flat collection branch) MUST pass `replay ?? {}` as the 4th arg so the inner `if (replay === undefined)` guard skips `acquireInstallLock()` re-acquisition. Otherwise the inner call deadlocks against the outer's held lock.

install-import-pickers-rule-7.rule: `install --sync` replay must reapply persisted `features` + `pick` from `installs.yaml` before validation/selection (not just the saved path), must carry through the caller's `--force` and related validation flags (never hardcode `force: true`), and the replay parser must accept persisted internal source formats (`github:org/repo@sha`, `blob/...` URLs), not only user-entered URLs.

install-import-pickers-rule-8.rule: `install --sync --dry-run` is not provably side-effect free — validate in isolated temp projects or inspect the implementation before pointing it at a live workspace.

install-import-pickers-rule-9.rule: Persist manual single-item installs by **parent collection path + explicit `pick`**, never the discovered file path. Pack names must describe stable source identity + normalized install scope (not first-picked-item naming). For broader-than-one-path identity, persist aggregated `paths` and match packs by repo identity + feature set so sync replay across multiple folders of the same repo/feature works.

lessons-system-apply-the-same-legacy-aut.rule: Apply the same legacy auto-migration gate before every CLI and MCP lessons read or write so MCP capture cannot strand legacy lessons.

lessons-system-await-async-transaction-m.rule: Await async transaction mutators while holding the lessons lock, or reject Promise-returning mutators at runtime and in the public type contract.

lessons-system-before-adding-a-flag-name.rule: Before adding a flag name to the parser's valueless/boolean set (so it stops consuming the next token), confirm no command reads it as a value — e.g. --version is global-boolean for the CLI but value-taking for 'plugin add --version <ref>'/install pinning. Restrict the set to provably boolean-only globals (json, verbose, help).

lessons-system-compile-command-pattern-t.rule: Compile command-pattern triggers at capture and validation boundaries; reject invalid regexes instead of silently making lessons unreachable.

lessons-system-keep-lessons-reference-do.rule: Keep lessons reference documentation synchronized with actual exports, ranked recall semantics, validation codes, and write-lock guarantees.

lessons-system-make-legacy-auto-migratio.rule: Make legacy auto-migration check graph existence under the lessons lock and refuse or merge when another writer creates the graph first.

lessons-system-make-public-legacy-import.rule: Make public legacy import refuse an existing lessons graph by default and require explicit overwrite intent inside the locked transaction.

lessons-system-preserve-every-occurrence.rule: Preserve every occurrence of repeatable CLI flags in the shared argument parser; do not overwrite earlier trigger values.

lessons-system-route-every-lessons-graph.rule: Route every lessons graph writer, including migration and scaffolding, through the shared locked transaction path.

lessons-system-split-lessons-modules-by-.rule: Split lessons modules by responsibility before they exceed the repository 200-line file limit.

lessons-system-treat-each-repeated-trigg.rule: Treat each repeated trigger flag as one opaque value; never split regex or glob patterns on commas.

lessons-system-when-testing-direct-legac.rule: When testing direct legacy-import overwrite behavior, seed the competing graph through the direct API so CLI auto-migration does not consume the legacy fixture first.

link-rebaser-deterministic-text-cleanup-.rationale: strip-markers' cosmetic cleanup regex mangled code samples in 11 lessons; caught only by corpus verification, not unit tests.
link-rebaser-deterministic-text-cleanup-.rule: Deterministic text-cleanup transforms over rule/doc prose that embeds code samples MUST be deletion-only — never reflow whitespace or punctuation. A cosmetic `replace(/\s+([,.;:])/g, '$1')` or multi-space collapse corrupts embedded code: `${{ ... }}` → `${{... }}`, `exit 1 ;;` → `exit 1;;`, `[ref]: ...` → `[ref]:...`. To strip a trailing marker that owns its terminal period, make the period part of the marker's own regex match (e.g. `\bSee\s+L\d+\.?`) instead of post-collapsing `..` afterward. Verify any prose transform against the real corpus and assert ellipses/fences/shell-punctuation survive byte-for-byte.

link-rebaser-rule-1.rule: Treat reference-style Markdown definitions (`[ref]: ...`, titled, angle-bracketed) as link destinations, not prose anchors — apply the same destination-relative rewrite contract as inline links.

link-rebaser-rule-10.rule: Preserve/add `./` prefix for same-directory descendant links inside generated Markdown (`formatLinkPathForDestination`). Assert the exact rendered path (`./skills/post-feature-qa/`) in tests, never "not canonical" loose matches.

link-rebaser-rule-11.rule: URI-skip patterns (`ssh://`, `git@host:`) must keep the scheme matcher distinct from Windows drive-letter detection — never let a single-letter scheme regex swallow `C:` and block legitimate absolute paths. Add same-file regression for both.

link-rebaser-rule-12.rule: Path tokenizers must require enough structure to distinguish file references from prose markers — the absolute-path branch must NOT match a bare `/` (e.g. `✓ / ✗` status text).

link-rebaser-rule-13.rule: Inline backtick path rewrites: tests asserting the rewritten form must accept any of `` `docs/...` ``, `` `/docs/...` ``, `` `./docs/...` ``, `` `../docs/...` `` via a permissive regex — Windows 8.3-shortname realpath divergence makes the exact form non-deterministic. The contract is "stable destination," not "always project-root-relative."

link-rebaser-rule-14.rule: `expandResolvedPaths` must yield the caller's `projectRoot`-shaped path FIRST, then the realpath variant as a tie-breaker — never `unshift(realPath)`. Realpath-first breaks `toProjectRootRelative` on DOS short names (`RUNNER~1` vs `runneradmin`) and symlinked tmpdirs. Audit every `[realpath, original]` loop.

link-rebaser-rule-15.rule: Import normalization must include BOTH the direct joined target path AND its `realpathSync.native` variant in the lookup map. Temp-workspace runs resolve through realpath and otherwise stay target-specific after import.

link-rebaser-rule-16.rule: Import normalization must build the rewrite map from every supported generated path family across ALL targets, not just the source target — re-importing a polluted artifact must recover canonical `.agentsmesh/...` links cross-family.

link-rebaser-rule-17.rule: Do not normalize bare root filenames (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.windsurfrules`, `GEMINI.md`) as raw substrings on the import side — they are common standalone words in prose. Only normalize when they appear in a structured path form.

link-rebaser-rule-18.rule: Any code participating in the link-rewrite map (key construction OR lookup) MUST use `pathApi(projectRoot)` from `src/core/path-helpers.ts`. NEVER import `join`/`normalize` from `node:path` directly in `src/core/reference/` or target-side `applyXxxRefs` helpers.

link-rebaser-rule-19.rule: Unit tests using a synthetic POSIX root (e.g. `ROOT = '/proj'`) with link-rewrite map machinery must alias `join`/`normalize` to `posix.join`/`posix.normalize` from `node:path/posix` — host `node:path` is win32 on Windows runners and silently mismatches the map.

link-rebaser-rule-2.rule: Preserve well-known canonical tokens (e.g. `.agentsmesh/`) in prose/labels/quoted/reading-context positions, but rewrite real Markdown inline-link destinations cross-format. Audit prose vs link classifier whenever formatter semantics change.

link-rebaser-rule-20.rule: After extracting helpers from `link-rebaser.ts` (e.g. `normalizeSeparators`, formatter helpers), scan every remaining branch (especially preservation/protected paths) for moved symbols and rerun the narrowest affected suite BEFORE expanding verification.

link-rebaser-rule-21.rule: Whenever the link-rewriter protection contract changes (fenced code, inline backticks, URI skips, drive letters), update both the main rewrite tests AND `link-rebaser-edge-cases.test.ts` in the same pass — the edge-case suite codifies the same contract separately.

link-rebaser-rule-22.rule: Reference-rewrite audits must search REAL canonical content for path patterns (including directory-form refs like `.agentsmesh/skills/post-feature-qa/`) and add tests for both exact files AND directory-form references. Synthetic round trips are insufficient — regenerate live target artifacts and grep the exact reported pattern.

link-rebaser-rule-23.rule: Generated Markdown demo content must use link destinations that resolve from EVERY generated target folder after rebasing. Keep speculative project-root examples as prose, not as clickable Markdown destinations.

link-rebaser-rule-24.rule: When parsing inline-link destinations with regex captures (e.g. `parseMarkdownLinkDestination`), guard the specific capture explicitly (`match?.[1] !== undefined`) under strict indexed access — don't rely on regex structure.

link-rebaser-rule-25.rule: Before adding extension-level skip gates in `rewriteGeneratedReferences()`, inspect the reference-rewrite matrix — supporting files like `template.ts` comments must still be rewritten; only token/comment-aware logic, not a blanket non-Markdown skip.

link-rebaser-rule-26.rule: Strict-prose assertions ("no leftover canonical mesh path") must run on prose with ALL rewriter-protected tokens stripped (fenced code, external refs, AND Windows absolute path tokens `/[A-Za-z]:[\\/][^\s,<>"'+'`'+`]+/`). The `WINDOWS_ABSOLUTE_PATH` guard in `link-rebaser.ts` is by-design.

link-rebaser-rule-27.rule: `shouldRewritePathToken` must split quote-like wrappers by intent: backticks (`` ` ``) are inline code and rewrite; single (`'`) and double (`"`) quotes are string-literal contexts inside code-like prose and stay verbatim. Don't restore the three-wrapper conflation in `link-token-context.ts`. When a canonical script needs a sibling file, author `Path(__file__).parent / "sibling.py"`, not `Path(__file__).parent / ".agentsmesh/skills/.../sibling.py"` — relying on the rebaser to "fix" the latter is the masking pattern this rule retires.

link-rebaser-rule-3.rule: Never inline `.agentsmesh/` as an exact substring in generated root-instruction decoration prose — reference-rewrite e2e strips fenced code and asserts the substring is gone. Phrase as ``the `.agentsmesh` directory at the project root``. Strip both old and new contract blocks on import.

link-rebaser-rule-4.rule: Add every emitted artifact path (including `additionalRootDecorationPaths`, multi-output families like Copilot's `.github/copilot/*.instructions.md` + `.github/instructions/*.md`, and Windsurf shared `AGENTS.md`) to the generate-side output-source map and build rewrite maps per output path / artifact family, not just per target.

link-rebaser-rule-5.rule: Pack skill artifact paths (`.agentsmesh/packs/.../skills/...`) must be added to `buildArtifactPathMap` alongside canonical `.agentsmesh/skills/...` so the rebaser translates both canonical and pack absolute paths.

link-rebaser-rule-6.rule: Shared artifact collision must compare canonicalized (un-rewritten) content, not post-rewrite bytes — collapse target-specific rewritten links back to canonical before declaring a true conflict. Keep target-native rewrite probes in protected fenced blocks or target-filtered fixtures so they don't poison shared outputs.

link-rebaser-rule-7.rule: Existence-gate rewriting: classify "should rewrite" vs "should stay unchanged because resolution fails" explicitly. Don't blindly normalize relative-looking refs whose targets don't exist (e.g. missing checklist refs, fixture `../SKILL.md`). Audit both categories whenever the link contract changes.

link-rebaser-rule-8.rule: For bare multi-segment paths under a root-relative contract (`src/AGENTS.md`, `docs/...`), resolve from the project root first, fall back to source-relative only if the root candidate is invalid. Add nested-file regression tests.

link-rebaser-rule-9.rule: For `../` over-traversal that escapes the workspace, retry resolution from the project root before giving up — real canonical files contain `../../../../docs/...` that still mean repo-root files. Cover in unit + all-target generate/import matrices.

shell-quoting-for-inline-typescript-eval.rule: For inline TypeScript eval scripts that need await, wrap the body in an async IIFE unless the runner is explicitly configured for ESM output.

shell-quoting-never-insert-zero-width-or.rationale: A zero-width space used to avoid closing a JSDoc block comment failed pnpm lint (no-irregular-whitespace).
shell-quoting-never-insert-zero-width-or.rule: Never insert zero-width or other irregular whitespace (e.g. U+200B) into source to dodge an accidental `*/` block-comment close — ESLint `no-irregular-whitespace` fails the lint gate. Reword the prose so the literal `*/` fence never appears (drop the inline example or describe it), rather than hiding a control byte in the comment.

shell-quoting-rule-1.rule: For inline Node scripts that use top-level `await`, use ESM `import` syntax; otherwise wrap CommonJS `require` code in an async IIFE. Never mix `require` with top-level `await` in the same heredoc — Node 24 emits `ERR_AMBIGUOUS_MODULE_SYNTAX`.

shell-quoting-rule-10.rule: Installer scripts that auto-edit shell rc files must key BOTH the rc file path AND the line syntax off the shell name. `export PATH=...` is bash/POSIX-only — fish rejects it. For fish, use `fish_add_path -gP "$BIN_DIR"` (or `set -gx PATH "$BIN_DIR" $PATH`). Always `mkdir -p "$(dirname "$config")"` before `>>` because `~/.config/fish/` may not exist.

shell-quoting-rule-11.rule: When parsing structured `<token>  <filename>` manifests (checksums, etc.) from shell, use `awk -v t="$TARGET" '$2==t {print $1}'` — field equality, not `grep "$NEEDLE"` substring. Substring matching silently breaks when filenames share prefixes (e.g., `agentsmesh-darwin-arm64` vs `agentsmesh-darwin-arm64.exe`).

shell-quoting-rule-12.rule: Validate env-controlled paths (e.g., `$AGENTSMESH_INSTALL`) against a strict allowlist (`*[!a-zA-Z0-9./_~\ -]*`) before interpolating into any line written to a shell-rc file. Otherwise a wrapping process can inject persistent shell code via the env var.

shell-quoting-rule-13.rule: When a build/test fails with parser errors ("Unterminated string literal", "Unexpected `<<`"), scan touched files for unresolved `<<<<<<<` merge conflict markers FIRST before deeper investigation — higher-level debugging on a syntactically invalid file is noise.

shell-quoting-rule-14.rule: When an `rg` search pattern starts with `-` (or may start with `-` after interpolation), pass it with `-e '<pattern>'` or place `--` before the pattern so ripgrep cannot parse the search text as flags.

shell-quoting-rule-2.rule: Never put escaped newlines (`\n`) inside a plain `rg` regex; ripgrep is line-oriented by default. Split into multiple literal patterns, or pass `rg -U --multiline-dotall` when a true cross-line match is required.

shell-quoting-rule-3.rule: Never assign to `status` (or other zsh read-only specials) in shell cleanup snippets — use neutral names like `rc` for captured exit codes. Verify cleanup ran when the sandbox/wrapper exits unexpectedly.

shell-quoting-rule-4.rule: For `rg` patterns containing backticks, `$`, or other shell metacharacters, use single quotes with `-F` (literal mode), or split into simpler literal patterns. Never wrap such patterns in double quotes — the shell command-substitutes the backticks before `rg` ever runs.

shell-quoting-rule-5.rule: For `execSync`/`spawnSync` calls that need shell features like `2>&1`, use `/bin/sh` (or omit `shell` and avoid shell-only syntax). Never hardcode `/bin/zsh` (missing on `ubuntu-latest`) or `/bin/bash` (not guaranteed on minimal images) unless the job explicitly installs that shell.

shell-quoting-rule-6.rule: For tests that need merged stdout+stderr cross-platform, use `spawnSync(process.execPath, [...args], { encoding: 'utf-8' })` and concatenate `result.stdout + result.stderr`. Never embed `2>&1` or hardcode any `/bin/*` once Windows is in the CI matrix.

shell-quoting-rule-7.rule: Never write a literal `*/` inside any `/* ... */` or `/** ... */` block comment — including JSDoc headers in test files. Globs like `skills/*/SKILL.md` close the comment early and produce misleading parser errors at unrelated lines. Reword to `skills/{name}/SKILL.md`, `glob: *.md`, or move into a `//` single-line comment.

shell-quoting-rule-8.rule: When a TS/JS source file needs control-character escapes inside regex literals, build the regex via `new RegExp('[<>:"|?*\\u0000-\\u001F]')` or `String.fromCharCode(n)` — never put `\xNN`/`\uNNNN` directly in a `Write` tool payload, because JSON evaluates them into raw control bytes before the file is written. Verify the resulting file with `file(1)` is reported as text, not `data`.

shell-quoting-rule-9.rule: When a fixture string needs literal `<<<<<<< HEAD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>>` lines at module top level, either (a) inline the literal inside a CallExpression argument, or (b) build it from concatenated parts (`'<' + '<<<<<< HEAD'`) so no source line begins with seven repeated `<`/`=`/`>`. TypeScript's lexer scans for left-anchored merge-conflict markers even inside top-level template literals (TS1185).

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-1.rule: Place every per-target `ImportEntryMapper` referenced by the descriptor object literal in a third file `src/targets/<id>/import-mappers.ts`. Never let `index.ts` import mappers from `importer.ts` and `importer.ts` import the descriptor from `index.ts` — the object literal will capture `undefined` for `map:` fields and silently break import. Create `import-mappers.ts` even when there is only one mapper.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-10.rule: When a target's `rewriteGeneratedPath` or layout references a constant (e.g. `CURSOR_COMPAT_AGENTS`), re-audit the `index.ts` import list at edit time. Treat missing-symbol `ReferenceError` from CLI generate as a release gate, not a runtime curiosity.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-11.rule: Single-letter URI scheme regexes (`^[a-z]+:`) must be kept distinct from Windows drive-letter detection (`^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]`). A scheme matcher that swallows `C:` will block legitimate Windows absolute paths from rewriting. Add regression tests covering both shapes in the same file.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-12.rule: In `resolveGen` and similar dispatchers with a plugin-registry fallback, check `getBuiltinTargetDefinition(target)` FIRST and delegate to `resolveTargetFeatureGenerator(target, feature, config)` for builtins; otherwise the plugin fallback re-applies the raw generator and bypasses conversion config (e.g. `commandsToSkills: false`). Do not let a generic descriptor lookup serve as the builtin path.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-13.rule: Never write a literal `*/` inside any `/* ... */` block comment (including JSDoc and file-header blocks). Replace `skills/*/SKILL.md`-style globs in prose with `skills/{name}/SKILL.md` or move them to single-line `//` comments. The same hazard breaks both production sources and test files.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-14.rule: When a command-orchestration test mocks `loadScopedConfig`, the mocked `ValidatedConfig` must include every field the schema defaults populate (e.g. `plugins: []`). Adding an orchestration step that reads `config.X` without updating every `mockLoadScopedConfig.mockResolvedValue` fixture crashes on `undefined`.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-15.rule: Do not mix CommonJS `require(...)` with top-level `await` in inline `node -e` / heredoc scripts under modern Node — it triggers `ERR_AMBIGUOUS_MODULE_SYNTAX`. Use ESM `import`, or wrap CJS in an async IIFE.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-2.rule: When auto-generating module-level data (e.g. `BUILTIN_TARGETS`) from per-target descriptor imports, patch the existing source file in place between sentinel comments `// <auto-generated:...>` ... `// </auto-generated:...>`. Do NOT extract the array literal to a new generated module — array literals evaluate eagerly and indirection through a separate file adds one more cycle hop that snapshots TDZ-pending imports as `undefined`.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-3.rule: Any lazy registry cache built over `BUILTIN_TARGETS` (or another descriptor-derived list whose own callbacks can trigger the cache during module init) MUST detect TDZ holes (`BUILTIN_TARGETS.filter((d) => d !== undefined)`) and refuse to cache until every slot is populated. "Lazy = safe from cycles" is false; lazy caches that capture mid-init state are worse than no cache.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-4.rule: Whenever a core type becomes a union (e.g. `McpServer` gaining a URL-transport variant), add explicit type guards at every serializer/generator boundary that requires a specific variant, and rerun `pnpm typecheck` before declaring the refactor done.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-5.rule: Read regex capture groups under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` only after narrowing the capture itself: `match?.[1] !== undefined` (or store the value first). Do not rely on regex structure to "guarantee" a capture; the type system does not.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-6.rule: Use explicit strict null comparisons (`!== null` / `!== undefined`). Do not use `!= null` shorthand — the repo lint gate rejects it.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-7.rule: Import Node platform globals (`URL`, `tmpdir`, etc.) explicitly from their `node:` modules. `URL` comes from `node:url`; `tmpdir` from `node:os` (NOT `node:path`); `join`/`resolve` from `node:path`. Ambient Node globals are not implicit under this ESLint config.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-8.rule: After any refactor that touches branch conditions, destructuring, helper extraction, or parsing/normalization control flow, immediately rerun `pnpm lint` AND `pnpm typecheck` — do not defer to broader verification. Sweep dead guard variables that fed the old condition; split destructured returns into `const` for immutable values and a separate `let` only for the one value that is actually reassigned.

typescript-esm-cycles-rule-9.rule: When extracting helpers, scan the remaining file for every symbol that moved and run the narrowest affected test suite immediately — do not assume "mechanical split" is safe. A preservation branch left over with a removed import surfaces as `ReferenceError` only at runtime.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-1.rule: In tests, import `runWatch` from `tests/harness/watch.js` — never from `src/cli/commands/watch.js` directly; mock the production module path separately while keeping the harness import.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-10.rule: When a watch test needs to wait for "the next regen cycle", thread an `onCycle({ featuresChanged })` callback into `runWatch` and assert on `cycles.length`/`cycles[i].featuresChanged` — never scrape `infoSpy.toHaveBeenCalledWith('Regenerated.')` or other externally-observable log/spy side-effects (the startup generate already fires them, producing tautological waits). Keep `scripts/flake-check-watch.ts` (N=10 under `COVERAGE=1`) and `pnpm flake:watch` wired in `package.json` to validate stability whenever the watch loop changes.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-11.rule: Any test that creates a watch then writes into a just-created subdirectory must force chokidar's polling backend (`usePolling: true, interval: 50`) via `tests/harness/watch.ts` rather than rely on native `fs.watch` — macOS FSEvents and Linux inotify drop events on freshly-added subtrees under parallel scheduler load. Keep production native for real interactive use; never trust kernel event delivery in parallel test environments.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-12.rule: Keep e2e CLI helper timeouts (e.g. `runCli` 30s) high enough for full-suite parallel pressure; reproduce timeout-looking failures both targeted and under the full runner before treating them as product behavior failures.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-2.rule: Watch tests that mutate files after `runWatch()` must first wait for an initial generated artifact or log signal, then perform the edit and wait for the expected reaction — never assume the watcher is past its initial generation/readiness phase under full-suite scheduler load.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-3.rule: `runWatch()` must wait for the chokidar `ready` event before doing the initial reconciliation/generate; verify both the isolated watch suite and full `pnpm test` after any watcher-startup change.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-4.rule: Watch-mode ignore filters must suppress both exact generated files (e.g. `.agentsmesh/.lock`, `.agentsmesh/.lock.tmp`) AND the canonical parent directory event emitted when those bookkeeping files churn; validate with the isolated watch suite and the full `pnpm test` run.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-5.rule: After bumping any test-runner or watcher-adjacent dependency (e.g. Vitest 4.0.x → 4.1.x), rerun the full suite and increase watch-unit `vi.waitFor` budgets again if needed — isolated green runs are not enough.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-6.rule: Keep watch unit `vi.waitFor` timeouts comfortably above 3000 ms (for example 8000 ms) and idle-stability delays at least 3000 ms — `pnpm test:coverage` slows chokidar debounce + generate past short budgets even when plain `pnpm test` is green.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-7.rule: Any watcher test must create a fresh temp project directory per test case; never reuse a prior watched path after teardown — shared temp dirs leak chokidar state under coverage load.

watch-and-test-timing-rule-8.rule: Never run test commands in parallel when they touch the same temp paths, ports, caches, or repo artifacts (e.g. fixed `ab-watch-cmd-test`).

watch-and-test-timing-rule-9.rule: Watch tests that prove event-driven behavior must keep the watcher in a `finally` cleanup and retry the triggering write until the observed callback fires or the normal timeout expires — chokidar may miss a lone create event under full-suite saturation.

windows-paths-rule-1.rule: **Never `split('/')` a filesystem path.** Use `basename(path[, ext])` from `node:path`. On Windows, `path.join` produces `\` separators, so `split('/').pop()` returns the *entire* path and downstream `mkdir` blows up on `C:/...` segments. Audit `split('/').pop()`, `split('/').slice(-N)`, and `endsWith('/x')` against native path fields whenever new path-derived identifiers land.

windows-paths-rule-10.rule: **Strip Windows absolute path tokens before "no canonical path in output" assertions.** The link rebaser intentionally leaves Windows absolutes untouched (`WINDOWS_ABSOLUTE_PATH` guard), so legitimate `\.agentsmesh\` substrings inside `C:\...\.agentsmesh\rules\typescript.md` trip naive `not.toContain('.agentsmesh\\')` checks. Extend `stripProtectedRegions` (or local assertion helpers) to drop `/[A-Za-z]:[\\/][^\s,<>"'`+`'`'`+`]+/g` first.

windows-paths-rule-11.rule: **Skip-on-Windows is the correct answer for POSIX-only test contracts.** Tests that (a) construct canonical content with absolute paths that turn into `C:\...` on Windows, (b) stub `git` via chmod-755 Node scripts, (c) pass `NODE_OPTIONS=--import=<windows path>`, or (d) assert POSIX mode bits (`statSync(p).mode & 0o111`) must `it.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')`. For mode bits, query the git index (`git ls-files --stage`) instead — NTFS doesn't surface execute bits.

windows-paths-rule-12.rule: **Walkers across project trees must skip `.agentsmesh`, `.agentsmeshcache`, `node_modules`, `.git` at directory-entry level AND wrap `readdirSync`/`statSync` in try/catch.** Windows TOCTOU between exiting CLI processes and test walkers ENOENTs mid-walk; the cache dir vanishes between readdir and stat.

windows-paths-rule-13.rule: **Bound symlink-based temp-project setups to dot-entries and root files only.** `createTempProjectRoot(homedir())` must never indiscriminately symlink Desktop/Documents/Downloads — `listScopedAgentsFiles` will recurse into them. Symlink only dot-directories (`.claude/`, `.cursor/`, ...) and root-level files. The same scope guard applies to `global` import: never run whole-tree `readDirRecursive(homedir())` for nested rule discovery; restrict to `~/.codex`, `~/.agents/skills`, etc.

windows-paths-rule-14.rule: **Cross-platform path fixtures must resolve in the real file tree.** Don't translate POSIX `../SKILL.md` to `..\\SKILL.md` without rechecking the file's actual directory layout — sibling references must exist in both shapes.

windows-paths-rule-15.rule: **`tmpdir` is from `node:os`, not `node:path`.** Stop the copy-paste before it lands.

windows-paths-rule-16.rule: **For inline-backtick path rewrites and any assertion that depends on realpath equivalence, accept multiple equivalent forms.** DOS 8.3 short names (`RUNNER~1` → `runneradmin`) make `expandResolvedPaths` and `toProjectRootRelative` non-deterministic on Windows tmp dirs. Use permissive regexes like `` /`(?:\.{1,2}\/)*\/?docs\/some-doc\.md`/ `` — the contract is "reaches a stable destination," not "always rewrites to project-root-relative."

windows-paths-rule-17.rule: **Tests that need merged stdout+stderr must not hardcode a POSIX shell.** Use `spawnSync(process.execPath, [...args], { encoding: 'utf-8' })` and concatenate `result.stdout + result.stderr`. Never embed `2>&1` or hardcode `/bin/sh` / `/bin/zsh` once Windows is in the CI matrix.

windows-paths-rule-18.rule: **Control-character escapes in regex literals must survive the `Write` JSON transport.** Build via `new RegExp('[<>:"|?*\\u0000-\\u001F]')` so the file stores literal escape sequences, not raw bytes. Verify with `file(1)` after authoring.

windows-paths-rule-19.rule: **Project-relative path validators must reject Windows absolutes independently of host OS.** Native `path.isAbsolute()` does not recognize `C:\...` as absolute on POSIX, so cross-platform canonical path validators must also reject `/^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/` before resolving against a project root.

windows-paths-rule-2.rule: **Pick `node:path` vs `node:path/posix` by path *format*, not host platform.** Any code in `src/core/reference/` or `applyXxxRefs` helpers that participates in the link-rewrite map (key construction OR lookup) MUST use `pathApi(projectRoot)` from `src/core/path-helpers.ts`. Never import `join`/`normalize` from `node:path` directly there. In synthetic-root unit tests (`ROOT = '/proj'`), alias `join`/`normalize` to `posix.join`/`posix.normalize`.

windows-paths-rule-3.rule: **Test helpers that fake `$HOME` must set `USERPROFILE` on win32.** `node:os.homedir()` reads `USERPROFILE` (not `HOME`) on Windows. Centralize the translation in the spawn helper, not at every call site.

windows-paths-rule-4.rule: **Normalize native-path test assertions through `toPosixPath()`.** `fromPath`, `srcPath`, and similar fields are intentionally native (callers pass them to `fs.readFileSync`); rewrite the *assertion*, not the production code. Use `tests/helpers/posix-path.ts` for `.toContain('.codex/...')` / `.includes('...')` checks.

windows-paths-rule-5.rule: **CLI display paths must be `.replaceAll('\\', '/')` before printing.** Tests assert forward slashes unconditionally; native `node:path` separators leak platform differences into user-facing output.

windows-paths-rule-6.rule: **Chokidar must use `usePolling: process.platform === 'win32'` in production, and force polling in *every* watch test on every OS.** Windows tmp dirs under `AppData\Local\Temp\...` miss `ReadDirectoryChangesW` events on freshly-created subdirs; macOS FSEvents + Linux inotify drop events under parallel suite load on just-mkdir'd subtrees. Wrap `runWatch` via `tests/harness/watch.ts` and always pass `{ usePolling: true, interval: 50 }`.

windows-paths-rule-7.rule: **Prefer the caller's projectRoot-shaped path over realpath; treat realpath as a tie-breaker.** On Windows runners under `RUNNER~1`, `realpathSync.native` expands to the long form (`runneradmin`), and `toProjectRootRelative(short, long)` yields `..\..\..` chains. In `expandResolvedPaths` and any `[realpath, original]` loop, the caller-shaped variant must win.

windows-paths-rule-8.rule: **Cross-platform repos commit `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf` and explicit text categories.** Don't rely on per-runner git config — Windows runners default `core.autocrlf=true`, rewriting fixture `.md`/`.json`/`.yaml` to CRLF on checkout while `writeFileAtomic` emits LF. For tests that stage repo files into a tmpdir, use `writeFileSync(to, readFileSync(from, 'utf-8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n'))` instead of `copyFileSync`.

windows-paths-rule-9.rule: **URI/scheme detection must not swallow Windows drive letters.** Keep the URI scheme matcher distinct from `[A-Za-z]:[\\/]` drive-letter detection. Plugin/source `isLocalSource` classifiers must accept `D:\foo` alongside POSIX absolutes — `node:path`'s `resolve()` produces drive-letter absolutes on win32. Regression tests cover both `C:` and `ssh://...` in the same file.
